'''Joseph A. Zasadzinski''' is an American chemical engineer and a professor of chemical engineering at the [[University of Minnesota]] where he holds the 3M Harry Heltzer Chair of Multidisciplinary Science and Technology since 2011.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://research.cems.umn.edu/zasadzinski/Site/Prof._Z.html |title=Prof. Joseph Zasadzinski |first=Joseph |last=Zasadzinski |publisher=[[University of Minnesota]]}}</ref>

==Education==
He received a Bachelor of Science in chemical engineering from the California Institute of Technology in 1980. He was award a PhD in the same field after working under the supervision of professors [[Howard Davis (chemical engineer)|Howard Davis]] and [[L. E. Scriven]].<ref>{{cite thesis |title=Liquid crystal structure by electron microscopy |year=1985 |institution=[[University of Minnesota]] |first=Joseph A. |last=Zasadzinski |oclc=223675095 |id=<!-- {{ProQuest|INSERT PROQUEST NUMBER HERE}} -->}}</ref> After receiving his doctorate, Zasadzinski spent a year as a post-doctoral fellow at the [[AT&T Bell Laboratories]].

==Career==

In 1986, Zasadzinski joined the chemical engineering faculty at the [[University of California, Santa Barbara]]. He left UCSB in 2011 to return to the University of Minnesota to join the faculty there.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/2011/05/110523152348.htm |title=New nanoscale imaging may lead to new treatments for multiple sclerosis |date=May 27, 2011 |work=[[ScienceDaily]]}}</ref>

Zasadzinski is on the editorial board of the [[Biophysical Journal]].<ref>{{cite journal |url=https://www.cell.com/biophysj/fulltext/S0006-3495(16)34289-8 |title=2017 Ushers in New Editorial Board Members and More |first1=Leslie M. |last1=Loew |first2=Beth |last2=Staehle |journal=[[Biophysical Journal]] |volume=112 |issue=1 |pages=E01-E02 |date=January 10, 2017 |doi=10.1016/j.bpj.2016.12.014 |pmid=28076821|pmc=5232859 }}</ref>

He was awarded the status of Fellow in the [[American Physical Society]],<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.aps.org/programs/honors/fellowships/archive-all.cfm?initial=&year=&unit_id=&institution=|title=APS Fellow Archive|website=www.aps.org|language=en|access-date=2017-04-20}}{{dead link|date=January 2025}}</ref> after he  was nominated by his Division of [[Biological Physics]] in 2008,<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=https://www.aps.org/programs/honors/fellowships/archive-all.cfm?initial=&year=2008&unit_id=&institution=|title=APS Fellows 2008|website=www.aps.org|language=en|access-date=2017-04-20}}{{dead link|date=January 2025}}</ref> for "applying physical principles of self-assembly, directed assembly and [[Biomimicry|bio-mimicry]] to create well-controlled [[lipid]] structures such as unilamellar [[Vesicle (biology and chemistry)|vesicles]] and "[[vesosome]]s" for biomedical applications such as targeted drug-delivery vehicles and treatments for respiratory diseases, and for developing new microscopies."<ref name=":0" />

==Awards==
* 1993 Burton Award of the [[Microscopy Society of America]]<ref>{{cite web |url=https://microscopy.org/msa-society-awards-recipients |title=MSA Society Awards Recipients |publisher=[[Microscopy Society of America]]}}</ref>
* 2004 [[American Chemical Society]] Award in Colloid and Surface Science<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.acs.org/funding/awards/acs-award-in-colloid-chemistry/past-recipients.html |title=ACS Award in Colloid Chemistry Recipients |publisher=[[American Chemical Society]]}}</ref>
* 2008 Fellow of the [[American Physical Society]], Division of Biological Physics<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.aps.org/funding-recognition/aps-fellowship?award_fellowship%5Bquery%5D=Joseph%20Zasadzinski |title=APS Fellowship recipients |publisher=[[American Physical Society]]}}</ref>
* 2013 Avanti Award in Lipids of the Biophysical Society<ref>{{cite web |url=https://avantiresearch.com/about-us/awards |title=Avanti Awards in Lipids |publisher=Avanti Research}}</ref>
